questions.question: ‘Mundari’ dance is associated with which of the following state?
questions.solution:
The Mundari dance is a traditional folk dance of the Munda tribe in Jharkhand.
  • It is primarily performed during festivals and harvest seasons to express joy and gratitude.
  • The dance is characterized by rhythmic footwork and is usually accompanied by traditional instruments like the Madal and Nagada.
  • Note: Jharkhand is known for several other tribal dances including Chhau and Santhali.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the dance form Lavani belong?
questions.solution:
Lavani is the most popular folk dance form of Maharashtra.
  • It is a combination of traditional song and dance, typically performed to the beats of a Dholki.
  • The dancers wear nine-yard long saris (Nauvari) and perform with powerful rhythm and erotic or social themes.
  • Note: It was historically used as a morale booster for soldiers during the 18th and 19th centuries.

questions.question: Which dance style is associated with the story of lord Krishna and his queen Satyabhama ‘Bhaamaakalaapam’?
questions.solution:
Bhaamaakalaapam is a famous dance-drama within the Kuchipudi tradition.
  • It was composed by Siddhendra Yogi and centers on Satyabhama, the proud queen of Lord Krishna.
  • The story highlights her longing for Krishna and the ultimate surrender of her ego.
  • Fact: Mastering the role of Satyabhama is considered the ultimate test for a Kuchipudi dancer.

questions.question: To which of the following states of India does the dance form Dandari belong?
questions.solution:
The Dandari dance is a traditional folk dance belonging to Telangana, specifically practiced by the Gond tribes.
  • It is typically performed during the Deepavali festival season.
  • Dancers wear colorful costumes and headgear decorated with peacock feathers, dancing in circles with sticks (Dandaris).

questions.question: Which of the following dances is performed by women on various occasions to the beating of a drum in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The Matki dance is a solo folk dance performed by women in Madhya Pradesh, primarily in the Malwa region.
  • The dancer balances an earthen pot (Matki) on her head while performing intricate footwork to the beat of a drum.
  • It is common at weddings and local festivals.
  • Note: Rouf belongs to J&K, while Bhagoria is a tribal dance of the Bhils in MP.

questions.question: Radha Sridhar is associated with which of the following classical dance?
questions.solution:
Radha Sridhar is a prominent artist associated with Bharatnatyam.
  • She is a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2018) for her contribution to the dance form.
  • Bharatnatyam is the oldest classical dance tradition of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Rukmini Devi is regarded as one of the most distinguished artists of ___________ .
questions.solution:
Rukmini Devi Arundale was a legendary figure who revived Bharatanatyam from its traditional Sadhir roots.
  • She established the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai to teach the dance with a focus on spiritual and aesthetic purity.
  • She was also a significant animal rights activist and the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Kathak dance is known as combination of __________ .
questions.solution:
Kathak is a 'total' art form known as a combination of music, dance, and narrative.
  • The word Kathak is derived from 'Katha,' meaning story; the dancers are traditionally known as Kathakars or storytellers.
  • It features complex footwork (Tatkar), rapid spins (Chakkars), and subtle facial expressions (Abhinaya).

questions.question: Which dance form originated in Andhra Pradesh?
questions.solution:
Kuchipudi is the classical dance form that originated in Andhra Pradesh.
  • It is unique for being a blend of Nritta (pure dance), Nritya (expressive dance), and Natya (drama).
  • Historically, it was a male-only tradition, but it is now predominantly performed by women.

questions.question: Which dance form from Karnataka involves large drums hung around the necks of men and is known for its religious and battle fervour?
questions.solution:
Dollu Kunitha is a high-energy folk dance from Karnataka involving large drums (Dollu).
  • It is primarily performed by the men of the Kuruba community.
  • The dancers wear the drums around their necks and beat them in synchronized, powerful movements, often depicting battle-like fervor.

questions.question: Giddha dance is mainly related to:
questions.solution:
Giddha is a popular folk dance of women in Punjab.
  • It is considered the female counterpart to the male Bhangra dance.
  • The dance is characterized by clapping (thali) and singing Bolis (folk verses) that touch upon social issues and daily life.

questions.question: _________ dance form originates from the southern Indian state of Kerala.
questions.solution:
The state of Kerala is the birthplace of two distinct classical dances: Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.
  • Kathakali: A male-dominated dance-drama known for heavy makeup and costumes.
  • Mohiniyattam: A solo feminine dance known for its graceful, swaying movements.

questions.question: Which one of the following dance form is performed by Kuruba men in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
As noted, Dollu Kunitha is the ritualistic drum dance performed by the Kuruba men in Karnataka.
  • It is dedicated to the deity Beeralingeswara.
  • The performance requires great physical stamina and strength to handle the heavy drums.

questions.question: Which of the following classical dance form is associated with Kerala?
questions.solution:
Mohiniyattam is the classical dance form strictly associated with Kerala.
  • The name refers to the 'Dance of the Enchantress' (Mohini), the female avatar of Lord Vishnu.
  • It is performed in a distinctive white and gold (Kasavu) sari.

questions.question: Which classical dancer was one of the youngest recipient of Padma Bhushan (1992) for her contributions to the field of classical dancing?
questions.solution:
Sonal Mansingh is a legendary classical dancer who was one of the youngest recipients of the Padma Bhushan in 1992.
  • She later received the Padma Vibhushan in 2003, making her the first Indian woman dancer to receive that honor.
  • She is a master of both Odissi and Bharatnatyam.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the dance form Chhau belong?
questions.solution:
Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial and tribal roots, found in West Bengal, Odisha, and Jharkhand.
  • The Purulia Chhau of West Bengal is famous for its elaborate and colorful masks.
  • It is recognized by UNESCO in the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity.

questions.question: In classical dance, which Rasa represents "Anger"?
questions.solution:
In the Navarasa (nine emotions) of Indian classical dance, Raudra represents Anger.
  • The other Rasas mentioned are: Shanta (Peace), Veera (Heroism/Valor), and Hasya (Laughter/Comedy).
  • These expressions are vital for the storytelling aspect of the dance.

questions.question: To which of the following states does the folk dance Khoria belong?
questions.solution:
Khoria is a folk dance native to the state of Haryana.
  • It is traditionally performed by women during the long wait for the bridegroom's party to return with the bride.
  • It features rapid circular movements and is characterized by a high level of energy.

questions.question: ___________ is a storytelling classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh.
questions.solution:
Kuchipudi is the storytelling dance form from Andhra Pradesh that originated as a form of Bhagavata Mela.
  • Dancers often sing the lyrics while performing, which is a unique trait among classical dance forms.

questions.question: __________, Which belongs to Kerala in southern India, takes its name from the mythic enchantress Mohini.
questions.solution:
Mohiniyattam takes its name from Mohini, the mythic enchantress.
  • The dance style is characterized by gentle, undulating movements of the torso, reminiscent of the swaying of palm trees or the waves of the sea in Kerala.

questions.question: Folk dance of 'Jatra' is originated from the state of:
questions.solution:
Jatra is a popular folk theater and dance form that originated in West Bengal.
  • The term 'Jatra' means a journey or procession.
  • It was traditionally used to propagate religious themes, particularly Vaishnavism, though modern Jatra covers social and political topics.

questions.question: Which of the following state is associated with Kathak?
questions.solution:
Kathak is the classical dance form associated with Uttar Pradesh (and North India).
  • It has three main Gharanas (schools): Lucknow, Jaipur, and Benaras.
  • It underwent significant transformation in the Mughal courts, where it moved from temples to royal gatherings.

questions.question: Sonal Mansingh is mainly associated with which dance style?
questions.solution:
Sonal Mansingh is an iconic figure proficient in Odissi (from Odisha) and Bharatnatyam (from Tamil Nadu).
  • She is also an established scholar and choreographer who has used dance to highlight environmental and social issues.

questions.question: Which dance style was kept alive by the Devadasis?
questions.solution:
Bharatnatyam was historically kept alive by the Devadasis (servants of the deity) in the temples of South India.
  • The dance was originally known as Sadhir Attam or Dasi Attam.
  • Historical Note: The form faced a decline during the British era but was revived in the early 20th century by E. Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale.

questions.question: Which of the following text is a main source for the study of the technique and grammar of body movement in Bharatnatyam dance?
questions.solution:
Abhinaya Darpana (The Mirror of Gesture) by Nandikeshvara is a fundamental text for Bharatnatyam.
  • It provides detailed instructions on Angika Abhinaya (body movements), hand gestures (Mudras), and eye movements.
  • Note: While the Natya Shastra is the primary source for all Indian performing arts, Abhinaya Darpana is the specific manual for Bharatnatyam technique.
